messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.099 atm), pure water freezes at roughly **–2.5 °C**.  
This is slightly below the standard 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm because the melting temperature of ice decreases as the external pressure falls.  

(For reference, at the same pressure water would boil at about 45 °C.)
